newsitem.title: CANADA: Market awaits next move by Canadian 88.
newsitem.headline: Market awaits next move by Canadian 88.

text.p: Canada's oil patch and investment industry were anxiously awaiting Canadian 88 Energy Corp's next move on Friday after securities regulators shut down trading in shares of takeover target Morrison Petroleums Ltd in connection with the C$652 million offer.

The decision by the Ontario Securities Commission meant Canadian 88 is unable to take up and pay for any Morrison shares by its offer deadline of today, and Canadian 88 must decide whether to extend the offer walk away from the table.
"These are exciting times," said CIBC Wood Gundy analyst Peter Linder.

In an surprise move on Thursday that threatens to scuttle Canadian 88's advance, the Ontario Securities Commission said trading would be ceased for shares of Canadian 88 in connection with the bid -- and shares of Morrison by Canadian 88 and West Central Capital Corp -- until Friday, February 14, or 48 hours after a decision from the hearing.

The OSC, Canada's main securities regulator, also said that a hearing into trading in Morrison stock by West Central in the time leading up to the bid would be moved to Monday from the previously announced date of today.

Canadian 88 chief executive Greg Noval was not available for comment early Friday, but in a phone interview late Thursday, he said company lawyers were working through the night trying to decide what to do next.
"We're still assessing our options," Noval said. "We've got to admire Morrison's tactic in holding up a bona fide offer to the point where investors can't tender into it."

The hearing was expected to probe whether Canadian 88's relationship with West Central, a private firm associated with the Calgary-based energy company, should have been more fully disclosed in the takeover circular for Morrison shareholders.

The OSC was also expected to determine whether all Morrison stockholders should be given the opportunity to sell their shares to Canadian 88 on at least the same cash terms as those afforded to West Central prior to the bid being announced.

Canadian 88 has offered C$10 cash -- up to a maximum cash portion of C$140 million -- or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share. Noval had said on numerous occasions that he had no intention of extending the bid, but on Thursday he conceded he may have no other choice.

Meanwhile, the OSC move has resulted in a sharply lower Canadian 88 share price, cutting the value of its share-swap offer should it decide to press on. Canadian 88 shares were down 0.45 in Friday trade to 5.35.
"I'm still convinced that there's another bidder out there and the bidder is looking better every day," Linder said. "His offer doesn't have to be nearly as high as it would have been a week ago."
